Title: 54,506 Muslim divorce cases recorded nationwide in nine months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 54,506 Muslim divorce cases were registered nationwide in the first nine months of this year, with Selangor recording the highest number.
According to Syariah Department data provided to Berita Harian, 44,603 cases have been resolved, 9,394 remain in proceedings, and 509 were categorised as archived.
Syariah Judiciary Department senior director (judiciary) Abu Suffian Abu Yaziz said cases categorised as resolved include divorces through mutual consent, decisions delivered after trial, and court-ordered dissolutions.
"However, not all resolved cases mean the couple is legally divorced, as applications such as fasakh can be rejected if the grounds provided lack basis and sufficient evidence under syarak," he said.
Archived cases refer to files closed for various reasons, including when applicants withdraw their bid or fail to attend court proceedings despite being summoned, resulting in the matter no longer being categorised as active or resolved.
Selangor recorded the highest number of divorces with 10,872 cases, followed by Johor (6,184), Kedah (4,727), Perak (4,038), Kelantan (4,004), Sabah (3,794), Pahang (3,748), the Federal Territories (3,698), Terengganu (3,663), Negri Sembilan (2,804), Sarawak (2,234), Penang (2,141), Melaka (1,878), and Perlis (721).
The types of divorce cases recorded include applications for pronouncement of talak before a judge (33,070), confirmation of pronouncements made outside the court (16,460), fasakh claims (3,712), taklik (1,161), and tebus talak (103).
Abu Suffian said a lack of awareness regarding domestic responsibilities contributes to marriage breakdowns, despite couples having attended pre-marriage courses.
"Some are not truly prepared to shoulder the commitments after marriage, particularly those relating to maintenance, children's needs, and the role of the head of the family. Upon marrying, they feel it is merely to satisfy personal needs without considering the obligations that must be carried out within the household," he said.
He said the court places emphasis on reconciliation or sulh before any decision is made in accordance with Islamic family law provisions.
Every application is examined under the relevant statutes, including Section 47 of the Islamic Family Law Act/Enactment, taking into account the grounds of the application and syarak compliance.
"The court assesses the grounds of the application to see if they meet the requirements of syarak. In many cases, reconciliation or islah is attempted first through the Conciliatory Committee and Hakam.
"If successful, the couple may reconcile. If not, only then will the court proceed with the next steps, including allowing the pronouncement of talak or rejecting the application," he said, adding that handling divorce cases has become increasingly complex.
The dissolution of a marriage is typically followed by ancillary claims, including iddah maintenance, mutaah, child support, custody or hadhanah, maintenance arrears, and matrimonial property division.
"From the perspective of the Syariah Court, the objective is not merely to dissolve the marriage, but to ensure that the process complies with syarak and the law, and that the rights of all parties are determined fairly, particularly regarding maintenance," he said.
To raise awareness about rights and responsibilities following a divorce, the department, through its Family Support Division, conducts community briefing programmes on marital rights.
Meanwhile, Selangor Chief Syariah judge Nenney Shuhaidah Shamsuddin said the first five years of marriage are among the most challenging periods as couples adjust to domestic life.
"This includes understanding the responsibilities and needs of a spouse. Based on my experience handling divorce cases, couples married between one and five years are among those most frequently facing separation.
"Couples who make it past that period are usually more stable because they have gone through the adjustment phase and begun to understand family life and obligations.
"People say the first five years are the most critical because there is so much to adjust to. Some marry for love, but when that feeling fades, they choose to divorce," she said.
She said divorces also involve senior citizens who separate at age 65, though such cases are far less common than separations early in marriage.
Among the main factors behind divorce are financial problems, followed by communication breakdowns and failure to carry out domestic responsibilities, with third-party interference ranking fourth or fifth.
Nenney Shuhaidah said the influence of social media has compounded the challenges, especially when oversharing about private lives invites external interference or scrutiny.
She said marital preparation should not rely entirely on two-day pre-marriage courses, arguing it should begin earlier through formal education on etiquette, responsibility, and family values.
"Exposure to the roles of husband and wife, parental responsibilities, and household management can be reinforced through school education to help young people understand family commitments before entering marriage.
"Relying on a two-day course alone is simply not enough. Those intending to marry should prepare themselves, but we must also consider how to instil awareness in our youth," she said.

Title: Fresh clashes rock France as protesters march on
Article:
PARIS: Clashes erupted across France on Saturday as protesters took to the streets, a week after marches that degenerated into violence and prompted a firm security backlash from President Emmanuel Macron, who is scrambling to restore order.
Police arrested nearly 1,000 people as officers faced "an extremely elevated level of violence" from black-clad "ultra-left" extremists, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said.
Riot police squads fired tear gas at protesters in the capital as well as in Marseille, Lyon, Bordeaux, Lille, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nantes.
Two people were "seriously" injured, Nunez said: one man in Toulouse, who reportedly had fingers blown off, and another person in Clermont-Ferrand. He did not give details of either case.
Authorities had deployed 70,000 security personnel across the country for the new marches, called to protest the cost of living.
The violence came a week after rioting that saw public buildings vandalised, hundreds of shops looted and 2,700 people arrested, casting a pall over the country six months before an election to choose Macron's successor.
Nunez said Saturday's outcome was more "positive" than a week ago, with more police on the streets acting more rapidly, conducting more pre-demonstration checks and better protecting businesses.
But there was widespread anger at the government over a protest crackdown viewed as an assault on the right to protest.
- POLICE BATTLE 'RIOTERS' -
Saturday's demonstrations drew between 410,000 and 800,000 people across the country, according to different estimates by authorities and the organising CGT union.
The main Paris march had between 110,000 and 250,000 attendees, according to those sources.
Macron's government has ordered police to prevent protesters reaching city centres, where shops are concentrated, and in Paris and some other cities, partial curfews were imposed in certain urban zones.
The French president had ordered non-union demonstrations be banned as "illegitimate."
In Paris, where many shops had boarded up windows to prevent looting, and the Louvre and the Musee d'Orsay museums shut for the day, the main demonstration passed off largely peacefully.
The march had been pushed to the capital's southeast rim under a last-minute order by authorities.
Afterwards, though, clashes broke out as the crowd was dispersing, with Nunez blaming "500 rioters" at the back of the march.
AFP journalists saw police charge several times, blasting tear gas and using batons against some, mostly young, protesters.
"They were just taking people down, you know, beating protesters," one demonstrator bleeding from a baton blow to his face, who gave his first name as David, told AFP.
- ULTRA-RIGHT VS ULTRA-LEFT -
Thousands of protesters in the western city of Nantes broke through lines of police firing tear gas and a water cannon to reach the city centre, an AFP journalist witnessed.
Emma, 23, who came out in the northwest city of Rennes, denounced the bans on demonstrations and the "repression" of protests by high school students demanding better learning conditions.
Marching in the rain at the head of the protest in the northern city of Lille, 47-year-old Delphine insisted: "Neither the president, nor the weather will stop me from demonstrating."
In Lyon, police used tear gas to disperse around 1,000 people gathered in the south of the city.
"If they ban protests, that means we're heading more and more towards a regime that is fascist, that is dictatorial," said one 20-year-old protester in Lyon, who gave only his first name, Silem.
In the southern cities of Cannes and Montpellier, far-right activists clashed with "ultra-left militants", in what authorities said was an unprecedented development.
There was looting on the sidelines of the marches in Marseille and Grenoble, police said.
The Yellow Vests, who staged disruptive protests against Macron eight years ago, called for more demonstrations on Oct 31 for "the freedom to protest."
Far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who marched in Paris, said the movement "is going to repeat itself every week."
- LE PEN PROTEST -
Tensions were heightened by a rally in the city of Orleans by far-right leader Marine Le Pen's National Rally party to kick off her campaign for the presidential election.
Thousands of counter-protesters chanting anti-fascist slogans marched in the city.
The unrest across France highlighted the febrile political atmosphere ahead of the vote, in which Le Pen leads in surveys.
Inflation in France, particularly affecting the cost of fuel, has surged since the start of the Middle East war in February.
"I'm going to try and instill a bit of optimism," said the four-time presidential hopeful, who has cast herself as the law-and-order candidate, ahead of her first major campaign speech on Sunday.
Protests have also broken out in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. --AFP

Title: Wawasan to consult PN partners before deciding on Melaka election
Article:
LARUT: Wawasan will seek consensus from its Perikatan Nasional partners before deciding whether to field candidates in the upcoming Melaka election.
Its president, Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainuddin, said the decision must be made collectively by all coalition members to ensure PN presents a united front.
"God willing, what matters most is the agreement among our PN partners.
"Only after that will we make an announcement. We do not want to announce anything prematurely, as the decision must be made by all PN members," he said when met after the Larut parliamentary thanksgiving feast held in conjunction with a wedding at the Sungai Bayor PDM Open Hall here last night.
However, he did not elaborate on the party's stance regarding its participation in the forthcoming Sarawak election.
Commenting on the possibility of PN taking legal action against the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over its earlier deregistration, Hamzah said the matter had been brought to court and should be left to the legal process.
"Whatever the case, we have taken this matter to court, so let the court decide," he said.
On Oct 22, the High Court granted PN's application for an interim stay against the RoS decision to revoke the coalition's registration, pending disposal of its judicial review.
The RoS had previously issued an order suspending all PN activities effective Sept 23. According to an RoS statement, the action was taken under Subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966 following a notice issued to PN on Sept 22.

Title: Sarawak records highest API reading at 192, 12 stations unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Twelve air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today, with IPD Serian in Sarawak recording the highest reading at 192.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Kuching recorded the second-highest reading at 187, followed by Samarahan at 183.
Sri Aman in Sarawak recorded an API reading of 159, while Batu Pahat and Pasir Gudang in Johor both registered readings of 158.
Kluang in Johor recorded 156, followed by Seremban in Negri Sembilan at 154, and Nilai in Negri Sembilan, Larkin in Johor and Paka in Terengganu at 153 each.
Kota Tinggi in Johor recorded an API reading of 125.
Meanwhile, 12 monitoring stations recorded good air quality, with Balik Pulau in Penang recording the lowest API reading at 20, followed by Kangar in Perlis and Alor Setar in Kedah at 23 each.
Other locations recording good air quality included Langkawi in Kedah (19), Kulim Hi-Tech in Kedah (32), Minden in Penang (31), Sungai Petani in Kedah (37), Kota Bharu in Kelantan (43), Besut in Terengganu (45), Taiping in Perak (46), Tanah Merah in Kelantan (47) and Seberang Jaya in Penang (48).
APIMS also reported moderate air quality at 44 monitoring stations nationwide.
An API reading of 0 to 50 is considered good, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and 301 and above hazardous.

Title: 109 foreigners arrested in Ops Gegar raids across Ipoh
Article:
IPOH: The Perak Immigration Department arrested 109 foreigners during two separate raids under Ops Gegar, including one at the Ipoh wholesale market early this morning.
Immigration Department deputy director-general (operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said those detained were aged between 19 and 59.
He said officers conducted the first raid around Ipoh at 9pm yesterday, while the raid at the Ipoh wholesale market began at 1.30am.
"During the raid, several foreigners attempted to flee. However, due to the efficiency of our enforcement officers and personnel, all of them were caught.
"Those detained comprise 34 women and 75 men from Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar, Indonesia, and Bangladesh," he told reporters after the raid at the Ipoh wholesale market.
Lokman Effendi said among the offences detected were lack of valid documents, overstaying, and abusing permits or passes issued to them.
"All detainees were taken to the state Immigration office for documentation and further verification before being sent to an Immigration detention depot," he said.
He said that following the operation, five summonses were also issued to employers and premises owners to assist with further investigations.
The case is being investigated under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Immigration Regulations 1963.
He added that more than 11,000 operations have been conducted since Jan 1, involving checks on nearly 150,000 foreigners.

Title: Delivery rider's death reclassified as murder after gig incident in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA: Police have reclassified the death of a 21-year-old delivery rider, who was severely injured during a gig at a cafe here, as murder.
Melaka Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Halim Abas said the incident, which occurred last Saturday, was initially investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code before being reclassified under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
He said the reclassification followed the victim's death on Oct 21, four days after suffering serious head injuries in the Oct 17 incident.
On the day of the incident, the victim was injured while at the cafe and taken to Melaka Hospital for treatment before being warded in the intensive care unit.
"However, the victim was pronounced dead at 3.53pm on Wednesday," he said in a statement today.
Halim said police have detained 10 people aged between 18 and 25 to assist in the investigation.
Police also found that the gig, held at a cafe in Kampung Jawa, had neither a police permit nor approval from the local authority.
"Police are still investigating the organisation of the event," he said.
The incident went viral on the social media platform Threads after the victim's death drew public attention to what happened during the gig.
It is understood that the incident occurred when the victim attempted a 'mosh' or spin kick during the music performance, but missed and fell, resulting in injuries.

Title: New York archdiocese agrees to pay US$800mil to sex abuse victims
Article:
NEW YORK: The Archdiocese of New York said Saturday it had agreed to a settlement in which the church would pay more than US$800 million to hundreds of victims of sexual abuse by clergy.
The agreement, to be formally signed in early November, marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the American Catholic Church has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s.
"We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors," New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks wrote in an email sent to his priests and forwarded to AFP by the archdiocese.
According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 victims will receive at least US$250,000, and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered.
The Archdiocese of New York, which covers Manhattan, Staten Island, the Bronx and several counties north of the city, will now be able to "turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children," Hicks' email said.
Hicks was appointed bishop last year by Pope Leo XIV, replacing the influential conservative Cardinal Timothy Dolan. Before his departure, Dolan had announced the creation of a US$300 million fund to compensate sexual abuse victims.
In the 2000s, press investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the United States had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities.
Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programmes have been created to compensate victims without going to trial.
Last June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay US$395 million to about 530 victims of sexual abuse committed by its clergy in order to settle their lawsuits. --AFP

Title: Expedite enactment of a comprehensive Clean Air Act
Article:
LETTERS:
The recurring haze affecting Malaysians should be a serious warning that we cannot continue to treat air pollution as a seasonal or temporary problem.
The current haze situation is once again affecting communities, schools, outdoor activities and the daily lives of Malaysians.
Several areas have recorded unhealthy air quality, while the authorities have had to consider stronger measures when pollution reaches dangerous levels.
I therefore urge the Government to expedite the enactment of a comprehensive Clean Air Act, with meaningful input from environmental scientists, public-health experts, legal specialists, industry representatives, local authorities and civil society.
Malaysia needs a stronger and more integrated legal framework to protect the fundamental right of our people to breathe clean and safe air.
Such legislation should not focus only on transboundary haze. It should comprehensively address air pollution from industrial activities, vehicles, open burning, construction, agriculture, power generation and other sources.
The law should also strengthen:
1. Air-quality standards and monitoring, with real-time information that is transparent and easily accessible to the public.
2. Pollution prevention and emission controls, particularly for major industrial and commercial sources.
3. Stronger enforcement and meaningful penalties against those who knowingly or negligently cause serious air pollution.
4. Clear accountability for polluters, including appropriate responsibility for companies and operators whose activities contribute to significant environmental harm.
5. Controls on open burning, supported by practical alternatives and stronger enforcement.
6. Public-health protection measures, especially for children, senior citizens, outdoor workers and people who are particularly vulnerable to polluted air.
7. Greater use of technology and scientific data, including satellite monitoring, emissions monitoring and early-warning systems.
8. Clear emergency protocols for severe pollution episodes, so that action can be triggered quickly rather than waiting until the situation becomes a public-health crisis.
At the same time, Malaysia must continue working with Asean partners to tackle transboundary haze at its source. Regional cooperation remains essential because air pollution does not respect national borders.
Malaysia has already proposed initiatives such as science diplomacy and a Sustainable Haze Fund under Asean's transboundary haze framework.
However, regional cooperation should complement — not replace — strong domestic legislation.
I welcome the Department of Environment's recent stakeholder engagement towards strengthening clean-air regulations.
This process should now be broadened and accelerated into a comprehensive legislative framework, drawing on the best available scientific, technical and legal expertise.
We should not wait for another major haze episode before taking decisive action.
Clean air is not a luxury. It is essential to public health, quality of life and sustainable national development.
Malaysia needs to move from a reactive approach to a prevention-based, science-driven and legally enforceable clean-air regime.
The time for a comprehensive Clean Air Act is now.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
Chairman
Alliance For A Safe Community

Title: 'Can't escape the burning smell': Johan Setia residents endure weeks of haze
Article:
KLANG:  A burning smell hangs over Kampung Johan Setia, where thick haze has lingered for weeks, leaving residents with itchy eyes, sore throats and coughs that refuse to go away.
For stall owner Nurarifah Fariha Huthfi, 35, the effects of the haze are plain to see in the customers she serves every day.
"Many people are unwell. I see many of my customers falling sick, coughing. Some have been coughing on and off for a whole month," she told the
New Straits Times
.
She said the acrid smell of burning was impossible to escape, even without stepping far from home, and was noticeably stronger in Johan Setia.
"Even right now without a mask, you can smell it, right? It has a distinct smell.
"And right now (the API reading) is only around 160. When it was at 192, your eyes would itch, your throat would itch and hurt... it was truly awful."
Nurarifah said she was not spared, working through a brief fever and repeated eye infections because she could not afford to close her stall.
"What choice did I have? If I take leave, my workers take leave too, and it becomes a headache!"
She said the haze was at times so thick that she could barely see, and the children in her family were repeatedly falling ill, including her 9-year-old asthmatic daughter.
She blamed the haze partly on the vegetable farms behind the village, claiming that some people took advantage of the hazy conditions to carry out open burning.
She said the farmland stretched deep behind the village, all the way to Bandar Putera Klang, about 6km to 8km away, and its full extent could only be seen by driving in with a four-wheel-drive vehicle.
Nurarifah, who has lived in Kampung Johan Setia since 1994, said haze was not new to the area.
She recalled severe wildfires there when she was a child, when the area was still dense forest and burning was common.
"Furthermore, it's peat soil. Peat soil is one of the hardest, once it catches fire, it's extremely hard to put out."
Despite the recent bout of itching, sore eyes and a cold, she said she had largely learned to live with the haze.
One of the farmers in Kampung Johan Setia, Hafiz Shaari, 65, claimed that his farm has sprinklers, insisting that open burning was no longer the norm in the area as the Department of Environment was keeping a close watch on farming activities.
Instead, he pointed to the rise of factories and warehouses on the village's peat soil as the cause of the persistent haze.
"As far as I know there are no fires," said Hafiz, who has grown vegetables there since 1995.
He said after 2000, industrial buildings had sprung up across the area.
"They have built factories, workshops, and storage warehouses.
"Before 2000, not much development took place, but now many industrial buildings have come up."

Title: Open burning fuel persistent Johan Setia haze [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   Open burning on farms and at illegal dumpsites is contributing to persistent haze in Kampung Johan Setia, Klang, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) has remained in the "unhealthy" range since August.
Previous reports showed that the village's API first entered the "unhealthy" range on Aug 8 at 153, before reaching 192 in September and again on Oct 14.
Village head Muhamad Zaki Che Deris said the 2,428ha village had extensive plantation activities.
Sungai Kandis assemblyman Wan Dzahanurin Ahmad said open burning, including on farms, remained a recurring problem in the area.
"The issue in Kampung Johan Setia is open burning, which also involves farms, including those run by foreigners, as previously reported in the press and raised in the state  assembly."
He said open burning was also taking place in nearby areas, such as  Kampung Sijangkang and Teluk Panglima Garang.
"The air quality problem in Kampung Johan Setia is also caused by open burning at illegal dumpsites in nearby areas such as Sijangkang and Teluk Panglima Garang," he told the
New Straits Times
.
He added that the area's peat soil made it prone to recurring fires.
Dzahanurin said Selangor Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin had told the state assembly in August that efforts were underway to flood the peatland in Kampung Johan Setia and its surroundings following frequent open burning.
"The Selangor Environment Department  and  local authorities have also  been carrying out monitoring and risk assessments at illegal dumpsites and around the peatland as a measure to prevent open burning.
"Peat fire prevention efforts have also received the support of the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department to ensure fires do not spread and that large-scale fires do not occur."
Dzahanurin said the haze was not merely a local problem.
"The haze affecting our country is not only a national issue, but also a transboundary disaster that requires diplomatic commitment between governments, as the problem stems from forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia."
Meanwhile, the Klang Royal City Council has stepped up monitoring and enforcement in the village following reports of open burning linked to agricultural activities.
Councillor Muhammad Azwan Adam said the council's Pantas Squad (Quick Reaction Team) was on standby round the clock,  focusing on late nights and early mornings, when illegal burning was most likely to occur.
The rapid-response unit, formed by local authorities and government agencies to handle emergencies and disasters, is focusing on agricultural and peat areas at risk of catching fire.
Azwan said every public complaint about haze, thick smoke or fires would receive immediate attention, with the squad sent to identify the cause and assist in initial firefighting, including tackling small fires involving shrubs and agricultural waste.
The squad also provides support to the Fire and Rescue Department and Department of Environment to ensure swift and effective action on the ground, he said.
"The public is advised to stay alert on the current situation, refrain from open burning and report any fires to the authorities immediately.
"Public cooperation is crucial to prevent fires from spreading, reduce air pollution and protect residents' safety."

Title: Trump casts early ballot as Republicans fight to retain Congress
Article:
WEST PALM BEACH: US President Donald Trump on Saturday voted early in his home state of Florida for the Nov 3 midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is battling to maintain control of Congress.
Trump and his wife, Melania, cast their ballots ahead of an appearance by the president at a campaign rally in the southern US state of Georgia.
Trump said he voted party line, or exclusively for members of his Republican Party.
Asked by reporters after voting about corruption as a major issue for voters, Trump insisted that it was happening in districts and cities controlled by Democrats.
"You ought to look at the real corruption – it's Democrat corruption," he said.
The Republican billionaire, who has consistently refused to accept his defeat in the 2020 presidential election, baselessly alleging widespread voter fraud, reiterated allegations along those lines Saturday.
"I ran and I won in 2016, and I won in 2020, too, but it didn't work out that way," he said at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office in West Palm Beach. "It was a rigged election, but I won by millions of votes."
With 10 days to go until the midterms, which traditionally favour the party outside the White House, Trump faces dismal polls suggesting the Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate.
Without a Republican majority in Congress, the 80-year-old president would have little room to push through his legislative agenda during his final two years in office.
He or his staff could also face numerous congressional investigations by Democrats, who have said they want to examine business dealings conducted by the president and those close to him through the family's holding company since his return to the White House.--AFP

Title: Thousands rally for Lula and Bolsonaro on eve of tight Brazil vote
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Copacabana beach turned red for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as hundreds of bikers revved their engines for right-winger Flavio Bolsonaro on Saturday, the eve of Brazil's nail-biter election.
Tens of thousands of supporters flooded the streets as the incumbent and his rival wrap up a bitter campaign that has left Latin America's biggest nation more polarized than ever.
Lula, who turns 81 next week, jumped up and down on the back of a campaign truck, waving a massive Brazilian flag as he made his way through throngs of supporters wearing the red of his Workers' Party (PT).
"The people must choose: either someone who kisses the national flag, or someone who kisses the American flag," Lula told the crowd.
Sunday's runoff will determine whether Brazil remains one of Latin America's few leftist nations or joins a regional lurch to the right championed by US President Donald Trump, a Bolsonaro ally.
Bolsonaro, son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, took a shock first-round lead with 47 percent of the vote over Lula's 45 percent.
"I think we needed that scare," actor Bruna Mascarenhas, 30, told AFP in Sao Paulo, Lula's stop after Copacabana in Rio de Janeiro.
"If we had won in the first round... we wouldn't have mobilised as much as we did," she said.
The political left jolted awake after the result, staging huge protests and launching an energetic digital campaign that hopes to carry Lula to a fourth, nonconsecutive term.
"Lula is essential for Brazil, for us to keep moving forward on social issues," said 29-year-old accountant Victor Gomes, who grew up in a favela and attributes his successes to the leftist leader's social policies.
The president "represents the voice of the most humble Brazilian people... who for a long time were not heard," he said.
A Datafolha institute poll this week showed the candidates tied with 50 per cent of voting intentions each.
- BIKERS FOR BOLSONARO -
Bolsonaro rallied a large crowd including hundreds of bikers sporting the canary-yellow national football jersey in Belo Horizonte, the capital of the key bellwether state of Minas Gerais.
Business owner Ebert Dorigo accused Lula's PT of seeking to make people dependent on state welfare.
"Our country is divided today because, due to welfare-based policies, some people... haven't grasped that improvement and achievement come only through hard work," he told AFP.
"Enough is enough. We've had 16 years of this administration, and it's clear it didn't work. It's time for a change," said Joao Paulo, 37, referring roughly to the total period the PT has governed Brazil.
Bolsonaro later headed to Rio to visit the house his father recovered in after being stabbed during his ultimately successful 2018 presidential campaign.
The senator took selfies with a group of children from the crowd that greeted him with US and Israeli flags as well as signs reading "Lula out."
- 'THE LESSER EVIL' -
In their final debate on Friday night, the rivals struck a calmer tone than in their first showdown, which descended into insults and was empty of policy proposals.
Lula attacked the senator's lack of experience while Bolsonaro accused the president of leaving behind a "broken country."
"He doesn't know what hunger is," Brazil's first working-class president said of Bolsonaro, who asked the incumbent: "Why are things so expensive?"
Bolsonaro has styled himself as a moderate version of his firebrand father, who is serving 27 years for attempting a coup after his electoral loss to Lula in 2022.
He has promised to resolve Brazil's crime woes, create 500,000 more spots in prisons and slash government spending.
Both sides leaned into fearmongering during the acrimonious campaign, producing a sense of alienation among many voters.
"If there were any other candidate, that would be a better option. But we're stuck choosing between the worst, the horrible, and the lesser evil," said event organiser Gabriela Ribeiro Viana, 29.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: MCA president walks out of BN candidate announcement over seat row
Article:
MELAKA: MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong walked out of the hall during the introduction of Barisan Nasional's candidates for the Melaka election last night, reports said.
Sinar Harian reported that Wee left the hall at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) amid MCA's dissatisfaction with the seats allocated to the party for the election.
Wee was quoted as saying that MCA had voiced its objections to the allocation and requested that negotiations continue, but the decisions were finalised without the party's agreement.
He also said the party would not recognise the announcement of candidates made without MCA's consent.
"If the MCA president himself has not signed it, how can it be recognised?" he said.
Commenting on his decision to leave the event, Wee said he was not there to express personal dissatisfaction, but to defend MCA's dignity and rights as a BN component party.
He also called on BN's central leadership to intervene to resolve the impasse, stressing that decisions on candidates should be made through mutual consultation.

Title: Melaka polls: BN candidates must work harder to win, says Rauf
Article:
AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) candidates contesting the Nov 14 Melaka election must work harder to secure victory in their respective constituencies.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said candidates entrusted to represent the coalition must prove their capabilities throughout the campaign.
"I hope those selected will work harder and more effectively to demonstrate their ability to win the seats they are contesting," he told a press conference after announcing BN's candidates at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here tonight.
Also present was BN chairman and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, along with party leaders.
Rauf said new candidates had been selected to give fresh faces the opportunity to continue serving the people, particularly in constituencies identified by the party as needing a change.

"We believe they can continue the various initiatives implemented during the previous term and introduce new agendas in the next term," he said.
BN announced 21 candidates, comprising eight newcomers and 13 incumbents.
Of the candidates, 18 are from Umno, two from MCA and one from MIC.

Title: Rauf: Melaka has no place for slander or hate politics
Article:

Title: Barbershops give Japan's yakuza their edge
Article:
AT a barbershop in Tokyo, yakuza gangster Tekisasu glances in the mirror at his meticulous new cut and thanks the hairdresser for the weekly trim crucial to his mobster trade.
Japan's yakuza operate an organised crime empire worth billions of dollars and have long dominated the country's drug rings, gambling dens and sex trade.
From precise haircuts to sharp suits, many mobsters try to project an image of menace and wealth, and barbers play a key role in crafting it.
"The yakuza are all about vanity," said Tekisasu, whose moniker means "enemy stabber", in an exclusive interview that took months to set up.
"The neater someone's appearance, the better his reputation becomes," said the 44-year-old active gangster allied to a major clan.
For Tekisasu and his fellow mobsters, barbershops also represent a break from the violent lifestyle they have chosen and an intensifying crackdown by authorities.
During his monthly, two-hour perming ritual — plus a weekly haircut that keeps the back and sides of his head shaven in a high "skin fade" —  the tattooed gangster can stop watching his back.
Yakuza numbers dipped last year to a record low of 17,600 nationwide. But even as their forces shrink, the gangsters represent
a potent threat, with younger groups of thugs brought in to diversify their business, police warned in a recent report.
Still, Tekisasu's barber,  who counts around 10 active yakuza among his repeat clientele,  had no qualms about serving them.
"All I do is make them look cooler," said the 32-year-old, denying there was anything wrong in making dangerous gangsters appear more aggressive.
Despite their criminal activities, many people —  including some of the gangsters themselves — hold romantic views of the yakuza's traditions, lifestyles and codes of honour.
The reality is often more mundane, with more and more rank-and-file mobsters said to grind out a living by targeting vulnerable people through crimes such as organised fraud.
Originally a gangsta rapper, Tekisasu delved into the yakuza world in his mid-20s, but was arrested in 2021, then jailed, before being released last year.
"I wish I could just live smiling, without hurting anyone or getting hurt. But that's not how things work in this world."
Yakuza face pressure to remain in the violent underworld, but they can and do choose to leave. An estimated 320 gangsters quit in 2024 thanks in part to efforts by authorities.
Under Tokyo's anti-yakuza laws, businesses are prohibited from knowingly "providing benefits" to mobsters to aid their activities.
Barbers who intentionally help yakuza clients maintain their looks are unlikely to violate the rules, provided the transactions are fair, according to retired anti-mafia detective Yuichi Sakurai.
But any preferential treatment, like "setting the haircut price excessively low", may constitute an illegal favour, he said.
In his decades-long career, the ex-detective noticed many mobsters "value frequent haircuts to retain their intimidating exteriors".
Far from being dismayed that gangsters frequent his parlour, Tekisasu's barber is proud that they trust his "uncompromising standards".
Following in the footsteps of his barber father, adept at a range of "bad-boy" haircuts, he has made punch perms his forte.
The tiny, rigid curls emerged in Japan in the 1960s and 1970s as a backlash against longer, Beatles-inspired male hairdos.
They have since found a devoted fanbase in manual labourers, teen delinquents and the yakuza.
"Punch perms are what I live for as a barber," said the gregarious shopkeeper, whose full-arm tattoos include depictions of scissors, a comb and a dryer.
While lore has it that yakuza gangsters found the punch perm's ultra-short length useful during brawls, Tekisasu said in his world, "fights don't usually involve hair-pulling".
"I simply like the punch perm because it's manly and cool."
Yakuza patronage involves risks, however.
"The last thing I want is for rival gangsters to run into each other here," Tekisasu's barber said.
The onus is thus on him to space their appointments apart.
But "once they leave the shop, whatever happens out there is going to happen. When they walk out the door, I don't talk to them anymore", he said.
The writer is from AFP

Title: Trump comes knocking on Kim's door ahead of Apec summit
Article:
AS world leaders prepare to gather in Shenzhen for next month's  Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit, speculation is mounting over a possible meeting between Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un —  a prospect experts say remains remote.
In 2019, North Korea's Kim made the 60-hour train journey home from Hanoi empty-handed after his summit with the US president collapsed.
Now, the dynamic has reversed: Trump is making repeated overtures, only to be met with silence from Pyongyang.
Trump said again last week that he "may" meet with Kim during his Asian tour next month and that it "would be exciting".
But on Monday, he said: "I don't know... I'm not sure that anybody's asking for a meeting,"  adding that his "relationship with Kim Jong-un is very good".
Any meeting between the leaders would trigger a media frenzy, but Pyongyang's deepening ties with Russia and China could complicate Trump's bid for a potential announcement of talks ahead of the midterms.
Analysts say Trump is seeking
a foreign policy win as the Iran war drags on. Kim, by contrast, may have less to gain from another high-profile encounter with Trump, they say.
Kim's decision to send troops and weapons to aid Moscow's
war in Ukraine has won critical backing from Russian President Vladimir Putin, helping North Korea blunt United Nations sanctions over its nuclear programme.
North Korea's economy, in fact, grew more than three per cent for a third straight year in 2025, South Korea's central bank estimated
in July, citing Pyongyang's "expansion of economic cooperation with Russia" as its major driver.
China remains North Korea's key ally —  a major source of diplomatic and economic support for the country.
"I see almost no possibility of a meeting," said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at the Institute for Far Eastern Studies at Kyungnam University.
"For Kim Jong-un, maintaining the status quo is the best option right now."
Trump met Kim three times during his first term —  once declaring they were "in love"  — in high-profile summits aimed at securing a denuclearisation deal, but no tangible progress was made. Since then, North Korea has continued to expand and develop its arsenal.
South Korea's dovish President Lee Jae-myung suggested in September that Washington seek a freeze of its nuclear programme in return for sanctions relief.
Critics say such an approach risks tacitly accepting North Korea as a nuclear-armed state while allowing Pyongyang to win sanctions relief without giving up its arsenal. Analysts say China appeared to move towards implicit acceptance.
Kim hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping in Pyongyang in June, soon after Xi held back-to-back summits in Beijing with Trump and Putin.
Neither Pyongyang nor Beijing mentioned North Korean denuclearisation in their official statements —  an omission experts saw as a sign of China's tacit consent.
The dividing of the "United States and Japan on one side and North Korea, China and Russia on the other... into blocs, is creating significant opportunities for North Korea," said Hong Min, a senior researcher at the Korea Institute for National Unification.
Kim's powerful sister, Kim Yo-jong, said in September the country's nuclear-armed status was "absolute" and called those hoping for its denuclearisation "idiots".
The more consequential question is "whether Washington would begin negotiating on the operational assumption that North Korea's arsenal is not going to disappear", said Vladimir Tikhonov, Korean Studies professor at the University of Oslo.
"I see that a possibility of such a policy shift is substantial."
Meanwhile, China's influence rests partly on its role as an intermediary between Pyongyang and Washington, and a direct Trump-Kim deal that sidelines Beijing in Shenzhen could therefore erode its leverage over both sides.
"A dialogue may be pursued with the understanding of Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping," said Yang Moo-jin, former president of the University of North Korean Studies.
But with Russia delivering immediate benefits, analysts said that time and strategic momentum are on Kim's side.
"Giving up all these benefits, withdrawing from the Russia-Ukraine war and entering uncertain dialogue with the United States is difficult to imagine right now," Yang said.
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Melaka must be developed by multiracial team, Malay interests safeguarded
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Melaka must be developed by a multiracial team that recognises the Malay community as the state's majority and a key pillar.
He questioned the point of winning elections by sowing racial hatred at the expense of the next generation's future.
"What is the point of winning by sowing hatred among ourselves? What about our children's future jobs and the quality of their education?
"How can we reach for the stars in new technology, artificial intelligence and the digital economy if we spend all our energy quarrelling?" he said at Stadium Hang Jebat tonight when announcing PH's candidates for the Melaka election.
Anwar also questioned why some quarters continued to resort to racial rhetoric, pointing out that DAP had not opposed policies to safeguard Malay interests despite being part of the cabinet.
"Why exploit racial rhetoric? When it comes to the Malays, we do more than talk. We approved Bumiputera land projects to protect Malay rights in Kuala Lumpur, and DAP is in the cabinet.
"We recently announced that government-owned land would be used to safeguard Malay interests in Kuala Lumpur, without taking land from the Chinese," he said.
He said DAP had neither protested against the move nor turned it into a communal dispute, questioning why the party continued to face attacks over racial issues.
Anwar said Malaysia remained one of the few multi-ethnic and multi-religious countries where people lived in relative peace, unlike countries where young people had taken to the streets over rising living costs and failed policies.
"Look at how many Malays, Chinese, Indians and Sikhs are gathered here together, reflecting our shared strength as Malaysians," he said.
Earlier, Anwar announced
PH's candidates
for 21 of the 28 seats in the Melaka election, which will be held on Nov 14.

Title: NST Leader: Fix dangerous roads before the protests
Article:
THERE are killer stretches on roads and highways all over the country, which may be the result of poor design. The danger is aggravated by drivers who like to take liberties with little regard for safety.
Whatever the case may be, those tasked to identify and weed out such killer stretches — be it local councils or the Public Works Department — have their jobs cut out.
News of some 100 protesters carrying a replica coffin and placing mock graves at an intersection along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari in Shah Alam, over a series of accidents involving heavy vehicles and a recent 12-vehicle pile-up on Oct 9 that resulted in four injured, dramatises the heightened public anxiety over this particular thoroughfare.
The use of coffins and mock graves in the protest marks a new low in public road safety and accountability.
When residents feel compelled to stage a "theatre of death" to draw attention to dangerous road stretches, it marks a damning indictment of the authorities' responsiveness or the lack of it.
No community should have to dramatise the prospect of death just to jolt the powers-that-be to take action.
This particular protest also highlighted the lack of progress over a proposal mooted as far back as 15 years ago for a 5km flyover that will address the recurring accidents.
We can cite many other cases over the past 10 years where Malaysians felt the need to take to the streets to demand remedial action.
In December 2021, Taman Melawati residents in Ampang picketed over stalled sewerage works that had left roads with potholes and damaged surfaces, posing risks to motorists and pedestrians alike.
In Kuching, residents living near Kuching International Airport have called for speed bumps along Jalan Sungai Tapang to curb speeding vehicles. A petition was organised in May 2024 to press the Padawan Municipal Council to act.
In Ipoh last year, Taman Tambun residents sought basic safety measures, including speed bumps, clearer road markings and signage at dangerous junctions, besides enforcement against speeding drivers.
In Kuantan, about 150 residents of Taman Balok Baru staged a peaceful demonstration in November 2015 against bauxite-laden lorries using and damaging residential roads near their homes. Their concerns included speeding heavy vehicles, damage to local infrastructure and risks posed to children.
The measure of good governance is not how quickly officials respond after an embarrassing protest. It is rather whether these officials act before residents feel compelled to stage any protest.
A road should not have to earn a reputation as a death trap before it receives urgent attention. It is incumbent upon officials to move from reactive crisis management to preventive action.
No Malaysian family should have to wonder whether their neighbourhood roads will only be made safe after a tragedy strikes.
A key part of any solution rests, of course, on budgetary allocations. The authorities concerned are clearly remiss if, after 10 years, no urgent effort is made to bid for funds to repair dangerous road stretches.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid expects corruption allegations to feature in Melaka polls, tells BN to fight back
Article:
AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi expects corruption allegations to feature prominently in the Melaka election campaign and has called on the coalition's machinery to counter them.
Zahid, who is also Umno president, said attacks against caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, BN, Umno and its partners were likely to intensify as campaigning gathered pace.
"I am almost certain the issue of plundering will be raised more frequently," he said at the launch of BN's election machinery at the Melaka International Trade Centre tonight.
He said the campaign would extend beyond the ground to social media, calling on members to use their accounts to respond to allegations against the coalition.
"Our battle is not only on the ground, but online," he added.
Zahid also called on members to publicise the state government's achievements on social media and distribute publications detailing its performance to households across Melaka.
"Our strength is an administrative record that the people can assess. Datuk Rauf's strength also lies in his excellent record of achievement," he said, calling on members to explain the administration's track record and plans.
BN will contest 21 seats in the election, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) will contest the
remaining seven
under an electoral cooperation agreement.
In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 seats, Pakatan Harapan five and PN two.
Zahid also called on BN members to maintain campaign discipline and refrain from spreading slander.
"We will not resort to slander in our campaign. Let our opponents do so, but it will eventually backfire on them. We will campaign with integrity," he said.

Title: Foreign woman dies after being found submerged in Tanjung Bungah condo pool
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 57-year-old foreign woman died after being found submerged in a condominium swimming pool in Tanjung Bungah today.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report about the incident at 6.10pm.
He said preliminary investigations found that the woman had been undergoing aquatic therapy with her husband at the pool at 5.20pm.
"Her husband left her for about five minutes to answer a phone call from a friend. When he returned, he found her submerged in the pool, believed to have fallen off a float," he said.
Abdul Rozak said the husband immediately jumped into the pool, pulled her to the side and performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).
However, ambulance personnel pronounced her dead at the scene at 5.49pm.
Her body was sent to the Penang Hospital Forensic Department for a post-mortem to determine the cause of death.
Abdul Rozak said preliminary investigations found no criminal elements. The case has been classified as sudden death, and investigations are ongoing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 9-month-old baby among four killed in Pagoh highway crash
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 9-month-old baby was among four people killed after the four-wheel drive (4WD) they were travelling in crashed into the rear of a trailer at KM107 of the southbound North-South Expressway near Pagoh today.
The accident is believed to have occurred about 5pm and involved a Ford Ranger 4WD, a Toyota Vios and a trailer.
Pagoh Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Hafiz Mohd Shahid said the crash was believed to have occurred when the Ford Ranger carrying the victims rammed into a trailer parked by the side of the highway.
"The four victims killed were two elderly women, a 5-year-old girl and a 9-month-old baby. Two other occupants of the 4WD were injured and rushed to hospital.
"Other injured victims were travelling in the Toyota Vios, while the trailer driver escaped unhurt.
"The rescue team provided initial treatment to the victims and cleared the accident debris. The bodies of those killed were handed over to the police," he said.

Title: Loke: Every ringgit recovered from corruption must benefit the people
Article:
MELAKA: The government will continue its fight against corruption and ensure public funds are not lost through leakages or waste.
Speaking at Pakatan Harapan's candidate announcement for the Melaka state election at Stadium Hang Jebat tonight, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said billions of ringgit recovered under Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration should benefit the people directly.
"What we must guarantee is that there are no leakages, no waste, and no corruption. We will fight corruption relentlessly!" he said.
He said he had proposed to Anwar that part of the funds recovered from corruption and misappropriation be channelled directly to the public.
"When we recover public money, we return it to the people.
"I recently suggested to the prime minister: 'Datuk Seri, can a portion of the recovered funds, money plundered or lost through corruption that is retrieved by the government, be channelled directly back to the people?'" he said.
He said recovered funds were currently channelled to education and healthcare, although the public might not feel their impact directly.
Loke cited the RM91 million raised from the special "H" vehicle registration plate series, which is being used to provide RM1,000 to each taxi driver.
"To all taxi drivers in Melaka, please take note: I will be coming down this Monday morning to disburse RM1,000 directly to each taxi driver," he said.
He said that savings from subsidy reforms were also being returned to the public through increased cash aid for the B40 group, tax cuts for the M40 and schooling assistance announced in the Budget two weeks ago.
"As a result of subsidy rationalisation, we save billions of ringgit in government expenditure each year. And every single ringgit saved is returned directly to the people.
"We assist the poor, we assist the middle class, we assist school children—we assist everyone.
"This is what we do, because we believe that we have been entrusted to govern, to safeguard this nation, and to protect our wealth and revenues for the welfare of the people," he added.

Title: [UPDATED] 'Green has accepted blue': Zahid says BN must embrace new allies
Article:
AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional machinery and supporters must embrace the coalition's new political partners and help their candidates win in the Melaka election.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said reciprocal support between BN and its strategic partners could pave the way for them to capture Putrajaya.
"Previously, we were allergic to seeing green.
"They were also allergic to seeing blue. From tonight, do not be allergic any more. Green has accepted blue. Blue must accept green," he said at the launch of BN's election machinery at the Melaka International Trade Centre tonight.
Zahid said BN's machinery and voters must support its partners wherever they contested, just as their supporters would back BN candidates.
BN will cooperate with Perikatan Nasional in the state election, with BN contesting 21 seats and seven allocated to PN. Zahid reiterated earlier today that
BN would retain the agreed seat allocation
.
In the 2021 state election, BN won 21 of Melaka's 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured five and PN won two.
However, Zahid said the arrangement would not compromise the coalition's principles or the identities of its component parties.
"Umno will never compromise the principles we have built together," he said, adding that MCA, MIC, PBRS, PPP and Friends of BN would remain important pillars of the coalition.
Zahid also cautioned against assuming that combining the partners' support would automatically deliver victory.
"Do not become complacent, thinking that by adding A and B, we can win comfortably. That does not guarantee victory."
On party discipline, he said BN's past defeats had stemmed from its own weaknesses rather than its opponents' strength, warning that internal divisions would give its rivals an advantage.
He urged those not selected as candidates to remain committed to securing victory for the coalition.
"Those selected as candidates must not become arrogant. Do not look after only your own group. Do not form your own teams or machinery that divide the party machinery," he added.

Title: PH banks on stability, prosperity and good governance in Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA: Pakatan Harapan is placing political stability, economic prosperity, public welfare and good governance as the four main pillars of its offer to Melaka voters in the upcoming state election.
Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the four pillars were essential to ensuring effective government administration and that development benefited all segments of society.
He said PH, which had long struggled as an opposition coalition before being entrusted with governing the country, recognised that power was a major test for any political coalition.
"When we are given the mandate to govern, political stability becomes the foundation for national development, followed by efforts to strengthen the economy and ensure the people's welfare remains protected," he said.
He was speaking at the announcement of PH's candidates and the launch of its Melaka election machinery at the grounds of Hang Jebat Stadium in Krubong here tonight.
Saifuddin, who is also home minister, said these efforts had to be supported by good governance, particularly in managing public finances to prevent leakages, waste, overspending and corruption.
"Do not allow funds to be siphoned off, do not waste money, do not allow leakages and never engage in corruption. Public finances must be safeguarded," he said.
On preparations for the election, he reminded candidates, party machinery and supporters to learn from the coalition's political struggles and continue working to ensure its proposals were clearly communicated to the people.
He said cooperation among PH component parties, PKR, DAP and Amanah, had to be strengthened, with each party supporting candidates from its coalition partners as if they were its own.
He said this spirit of solidarity was important to ensure the entire election machinery worked in a coordinated manner.
Saifuddin expressed confidence that PH stood a chance of achieving a better result in the coming election if all its component parties and election machinery worked together with the same fighting spirit.

Title: Police record statements from 4 witnesses in boy's fatal fall
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police have recorded statements from four witnesses following the death of a 7-year-old boy who fell from the 10th floor of a flat in Taman Perling yesterday.
Acting Johor Baru Utara district police chief Superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor said initial investigations indicated that the boy had been playing with several other children along the 10th-floor corridor before the incident.
He said the boy was believed to have used a bicycle to climb over the corridor wall before falling.
"The boy was found on the ground below the flat by residents at 5.30pm on Oct 23.
"He sustained serious injuries to his head, hands and body and was pronounced dead by a medical officer from Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA), Johor Baru, who arrived at the scene," he said in a statement today.
Azrol said a post-mortem conducted at 11am confirmed that the cause of death was multiple injuries sustained in a fall from height.
He said the case had been classified as sudden death and investigations were ongoing.
The boy, Mohammad Adib Rizqy Mohammad Fauzi, was a Primary One pupil at SK Tampoi Utama and the second of four siblings.
At the time of the incident, he had been riding his bicycle outside his home while his mother was tidying the house and his father was at work.
Azrol advised parents and guardians to monitor their children closely to prevent similar incidents.
He also urged them to ensure children did not climb or play near windows, balconies, corridors or other high-risk areas that could result in serious injury or death.
Anyone with information about the incident can contact the Johor Baru Utara district police headquarters hotline at 07-556 3122 to assist with investigations.

Title: Azmin denies Bersatu supports appeal against PN deregistration stay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali has denied claims that the party supports the government's appeal against a High Court decision staying Perikatan Nasional's deregistration.
In a Facebook post today, Azmin said a statement claiming that Bersatu supported the Home Minister's move to appeal the ruling was fake.
"Slander. Fake," he wrote, attaching an image of the purported statement.
It was reported yesterday that the Registrar of Societies (RoS) and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had filed an appeal against the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision to stay PN's deregistration. (hyperlink: https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1561922/updated-govt-appeals-high-court-ruling-allowing-pn-resume-activities )
On Thursday, the High Court granted a stay of the deregistration pending a judicial review, allowing the coalition to contest the Nov 14 Melaka election using its logo. (hyperlink: https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1561363/updated-high-court-grants-pn-stay-ros-deregistration )
The RoS had revoked PN's registration on Tuesday after finding that the coalition's explanation had failed to address the grounds for deregistration. (hyperlink:https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1559456/updated-ros-confirms-pns-deregistration )
Following the decision, Azmin said the deregistration vindicated Bersatu's earlier complaint against PN's leadership over alleged breaches of the coalition's constitution. (hyperlink: https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1559594/updated-azmin-denying-bersatu-rights-pn-meeting-led-deregistration)
